text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because it usually has no symptoms. Most people can live with high blood pressure for years without feeling any warning signs or changes.
Symptoms generally do not appear until blood pressure becomes dangerously high—such as during a severe spike or a hypertensive crisis. When symptoms do show up, they may include:

list.snippet: Vision changes (such as blurred or double vision)
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Nosebleeds or tiny blood spots in the eyes

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do in a Hypertensive Emergency
According to the American Heart Association:

list.snippet: If your blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg, wait one minute and test it again.

If the second reading is still over 180/120 mm Hg and you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, vision changes, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
If you have no symptoms at that reading level, contact your healthcare professional right away for guidance.

text_blocks.snippet: Because high blood pressure has no reliable physical clues for most people, regular blood pressure checks at home or with a doctor are the only way to catch it early.
